entry_sequence.action: we're going to get to our desks right at 9:30 a.m. EST
we're going to wait for the first candle of the day at that 9:30 time to print
We're going to start on our five-minute chart.
then we're going to mark out the high and the low of that first 5-minute candle that happens at 9:30 to 9:35 a.m. Eastern Standard Time
we are going to switch to the 1 minute chart
we're going to wait for a break of the level, but we need a fair value gap
we want to wait for a retest of the fair value gap. Meaning we need the market to trade back into the fair value gap.
after we've traded into the fair value gap, then we wait for this retest candle right here to get engulfed
as soon as we get this engulfing, you're good to enter the trade
you're going to start on the 15minute chart
We're going to wait until the 9:30 to 9:45 Eastern Standard Time candle closes. So, it's still the first candle of the day. It's just using the 15minute instead.
we're going to mark the high and the low of the first 15-minute candle
Instead of going to the one minute chart, we're going to go to the five-minute chart.
we have now created our fair value gap through this first candle
instead of waiting for a retest, we're actually going to set a limit order on the FVG. This means once the market trades back into the fair value gap, we're automatically entered into the market.

confluences.description: This strategy works for any market, whether it's futures, stocks, crypto, or forex, and you use the same time for each market.
since we broke through the high, the direction is bullish. We're going to be looking for long trades.
Simply crossing through the level, whether it's a wick or a candle closure, just won't cut it.
a fair value gap is just a three candle formation where we leave a gap between one candle's wick and the third candle's wick
the middle candle was very expansive, showing a lot of force, which tells us that buyers are in control, especially when it happens through this first 5-minute candle level
if you're not aware of what an engulfing is, it's when the body of one candle gets completely closed through by opposing direction candles
every once in a while, you're going to have the market come down and revisit the fair value gap. That's totally fine.

stop.scalping: you want to put that under the lowest area that we traded into that fair value gap. And you always want to give it one tick of breathing room.
stop.day_trading: I'm going to put it right at the first candle in the fair value gap pattern. Remember a fair value gap is three candles. So it goes right under this first one.

targets.description: we are just targeting a fixed 3:1 return, meaning that on our winning trades, we make three times as much profit as we would lose on a losing trade.
instead of a 3 to one return we are going to target a fixed 2:1 return
